reel.caption:
Bought a bike on EMI at "6% flat": why does it cost you ₹8,481 more?

A flat rate charges interest on the full loan for the whole tenure, even as you repay it.
Illustrative ₹1 lakh for 3 years at 6% flat: interest ₹18,000 (EMI ≈ ₹3,278).
The same loan at a real 6% on the reducing balance: interest ≈ ₹9,519 (EMI ≈ ₹3,042).
That's ≈ ₹8,481 more, and the flat loan's true yearly rate works out to about 11%.
Illustrative; fees, GST on fees and your lender's terms change the real figure. Ask for the reducing-balance rate before you sign.

Was your vehicle loan quoted as a flat rate or a reducing rate?

Sources: a private bank's explainer on flat vs reducing-balance EMI formulas; a lender's flat vs reducing rate guide with a worked example (Mar 2026). Figures calculated from those formulas. Illustrative only.
